        ### Question
        You are seeing a 4-year-old boy in clinic who is presenting with concern for a primary immune deficiency. He has an unremarkable birth history, but since the age of 6 months he has had recurrent otitis media, bacterial pneumonia, as well as two episodes of sinusitis, and four episodes of conjunctivitis. He has a maternal uncle who died from sepsis secondary to H. influenza pneumonia. If you drew blood work for diagnostic testing, which of the following would you expect to find?

        ### Options
        opa. Abnormally low number of B cells
opb. Abnormally low number of T cells
opc. Abnormally high number of B cells
opd. Abnormally high number of T cells
ope. Elevated immunoglobulin levels

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Recurrent otitis media, bacterial pneumonia, sinusitis, and conjunctivitis -> Suspected primary immune deficiency -> Consider immune system evaluation -> 80% CHAIN: Family history of sepsis secondary to H. influenza pneumonia -> Suspected genetic predisposition to infections -> Consider immune system evaluation -> 75% CHAIN: Maternal uncle died from sepsis secondary to H. influenza pneumonia -> Suspected genetic susceptibility to specific pathogens -> Consider immune system evaluation -> 70% CHAIN: Recurrent infections since 6 months of age -> Suggestive of underlying immune dysfunction -> Consider immune system evaluation -> 85% CHAIN: Recurrent infections despite unremarkable birth history -> Indicative of acquired immune deficiency -> Consider immune system evaluation -> 80%
